Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mrs. Justice P. Sree Sudha
 Oral Judgment

1. This appeal is filed by the claimant against the judgment and award dated 19.09.2022 passed by the IV Additional Senior Civil Judge and Member, M.A.C.T.-XV Vijayapura [for short 'Tribunal'] in MVC No.642/2019 seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. The injured claimant aged 24 years, met with a road traffic accident on 27.06.2018 and sustained grievous injuries.
Hence, he filed claim petition before the Tribunal seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/-.

The Tribunal after considering the entire evidence on record, awarded the compensation of Rs.4,67,600/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization and NC: 2025:KHC-K:6792 HC-KAR directed respondent No.2-Insurance Company to pay the compensation.
Aggrieved by the said order, this appeal is preferred.

3. Heard arguments of both the parties and perused the materials available on record.
4.
The main contention of the claimant is that the Tribunal has awarded meagre compensation under all heads.

It is contended by the learned counsel for the appellant that the claimant has examined the Orthopaedic Surgeon as PW2, who has deposed that the injuries have affected right lower limb and difficulties in squatting, kneeling, sitting cross leg; standing on operated limb for long time, stability component constitutes 9% disability, right thigh muscles wasting compare to left 5% disability and assessed 22% to 24% disability to right lower limb, but the Tribunal has taken only 5% disability to the while body.

It is also contended that claimant was earning Rs.15,000/- per month, but the Tribunal has not considered the same and thus, requested for enhancing NC:
2025:KHC-K:6792 HC-KAR the compensation with 9% interest per annum instead of 6%.

2 5.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 - Insurance Company that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and needs no interference.
Appellant was admitted to the hospital on 26.06.2018 and discharged on 16.07.2018.
Thus, he was inpatient for 20 days.

PW2 - Doctor issued Ex.P16 - Disability Certificate stating 22% to 24%
disability to right lower limb.

Considering the evidence of the Doctor and other relevant material,
this Court finds it reasonable to NC: 2025:KHC-K:6792 HC-KAR consider 15% disability to whole body instead of 5% taken by the Tribunal.
7. Further, though, the claimant states that he was earning Rs.15,000/- per month, he has not produced any document to prove the same.
Accident is of the year 2018.

As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, the Tribunal has rightly taken the notional income of the claimant at Rs.11,750/- per month for the year 2018, which needs no interference.

Accordingly, the claimant is entitled for loss of future earning as under:
Rs.11,750/- x 12 x 18x 15% = Rs.3,80,700/-
8.

Considering the period of hospitalization, nature of injuries and other relevant factors, this Court finds it reasonable to award an amount of Rs.75,000/- for pain and suffering, Rs.25,000/- for loss of amenities and Rs.30,000/- for transportation, extra nourishment and attendant charges.

Further,
due to injuries the claimant NC: 2025:KHC-K:6792 HC-KAR might not have attended any work atleast for a period of 4 months, hence, this Court finds it reasonable to award Rs.47,000/- for loss of income during laid up period.
However, the compensation of Rs.2,63,294/- awarded by the Tribunal for medical expenses, needs no interference.

9. The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is modified as under:

Rs.75,000/-
suffering 2

Medical Rs.2,63,294/- Rs.2,63,294/-

There will be enhancement of Rs.3,53,408/-
10.
Respondent No.2 - Insurance Company has already deposited the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal.

11. In the result, the following order is passed:
 (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
 (ii) The claimant is entitled for the enhanced compensation of Rs.3,53,408/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.

(iii) Respondent No.2 - Insurance Company is directed to deposit the aforesaid NC:
2025:KHC-K:6792 HC-KAR compensation amount along with interest within one month from the date of this judgment.
(iv) On such deposit, the claimant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with interest accrued on it.
